sources.excerpt: Skreddy Kusanagi Fuzz | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Skreddy Kusanagi Fuzz Updated Jun. 16, 2015  |  by Paolo De Gregorio The Tone Bender is one of the most legendary effects in guitar history, and for good reason. The signature fuzz sound it produced inspired a generation of burgeoning rock guitarists. It was a notoriously fickle design though, using rare components and positive ground connection (almost all effects are negative-ground power). Skreddy Pedals has introduced a fuzz pedal, called Kusanagi , that remains true to the original circuit design (circa 1966) while including additional, updated features. Many of the esoteric electronic components are included, such as larger carbon resistors, axial capacitors and germanium transistors. While the Tone Benders of yesteryear featured positive ground power, the Kusanagi features pedalboard-friendly negative-ground power and can be run off of the adapter or a 9v battery. The Skreddy also features true bypass switching and top-mounted input/output jack in a solid enclosure. There are 3 controls. Level adjusts the output, attack serves as input gain, and the gate control adjusts the bias and allows for fine-tuning of the fuzz sound. The Kusanagi from Skreddy Effects is a fresh take on a classic design. – Brandon Stoner Related Delicious Audio Posts: Fjord Fuzz Thor Fuzz Fjord Fuzz Dovre Fuzz + Reverb Fjord Fuzz Sol Fuzz + Vibe New Pedal: Mad Professor Milestone Fuzz Dazatronyx Big Fuzz Console Updated Pedal: Mattoverse AirTrash MkII Fuzz Categories: FUZZ PEDALS Tags: 3-transistor | Germanium | kusanagi | Pedals | skreddy | tone bender Previous post Big Knob's Wah Fix Next post Bowmont's Gear, Synths and Creative Process Post Your Comment Here Comment Name required Author Email required Email Website Search XHTML: You can use these tags: <a href="" title=""> <abbr title=""> <acronym title=""> <b> <blockquote cite=""> <cite> <code> <del datetime=""> <em> <i> <q cite=""> <s> <strike> <strong> --> Click here to cancel reply. -->   -->         Best Reverb Pedals: A Complete Guide Best Delay Pedals: A Complete Guide Best Klon Clones   The Best Uni-Vibe Pedals: Clones, Evolutions, Stereo Vibes ,   Browse All Our Pedal Guides   © Delicious Audio | All Rights Reserved. | About us + Contact Info | Affiliate Links in USD, CAD, Euro & Pound Help Support the Site |
